title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building the 'déploiement' (unfolding) of a stratified space Σ. He uses a system of spaces Σ^*(n), with Σ^*(0) = Σ, and simplicial operators between them. Σ^*(1) is a space whose points over x ∈ Σ are the local codimension-1 boundary germs B_α at x. Locally the picture is that of a manifold with corners whose corner faces are ordered. The previous page set out conditions b1–b3. If x has n boundary germs, there is a unique x̃ ∈ Σ^*(n) over x whose n face images are the z_α. For 1 ≤ d ≤ n, the points of Σ^*(d) over x correspond bijectively to the d-element subsets A of I = {z_α}, identified with {0,…,n−1}.

This page finishes b3. To a subset A one attaches the unique increasing map Δ_d = {0,…,d} → Δ_n = {0,…,n} with image A ∪ {n}. The corresponding simplicial map Σ^*(n) → Σ^*(d) sends x̃ to the point z of Σ^*(d) attached to A. Composing with the map induced by {d} ↪ Δ_d gives the projection Σ^*(d) → Σ^*(0), which sends z to x.

Moreover, for z ∈ Σ^*(d) over x, the image of the germ of Σ^*(d) at z in the germ of Σ at x is exactly the intersection of the boundary germs B_α for z_α ∈ A. In modern terms, Σ^*(d) is the d-fold corner/boundary space ∂^d Σ: points are x together with d local boundary components. It maps onto the codimension-d corner strata.

Next Grothendieck keeps only the morphisms Δ_d → Δ_d' that are strictly increasing and cofinal, i.e. preserve the last element. He notes that the category of nonempty finite totally ordered sets with such maps is equivalent to the category of all finite totally ordered sets, possibly empty, with strictly increasing maps. The equivalence is d ↦ d ⊔ {ω}, adjoining a new last element ω, with ω ↦ ω on maps. Hence Γ: d ↦ Σ^*(d ⊔ {ω}) is a (contravariant) functor on finite ordered sets including ∅, with injective monotone maps. That is, Γ is an augmented semi-simplicial space with Γ(∅) = Σ^*(0) = Σ, and Γ(n) = Σ^*(n+1) in the margin's indexing.

The page breaks off at: giving Γ amounts to giving Γ(∅) and a semi-simplicial space over it. The next page interprets this: b1–b3 say this relative semi-simplicial space comes from a locally cylindrical stratification of Σ whose codimension-1 strata through each point are ordered, continuously in x. Γ(d) is the space of germs of codimension-(d+1) strata, and the face maps come from the ordering. Over each point x, the fibre of Γ is the full simplex on the set of local boundary germs; Γ(k) has fibre the (k+1)-subsets. So the structure is a 'family of simplices', the combinatorial skeleton of the corner structure. Its purpose is to rebuild the unfolding spaces from Σ.
errors: Γ should be contravariant on strictly increasing maps (a presheaf / augmented semi-simplicial object); calling it a 'foncteur' without specifying variance is a minor imprecision.
Indexing shifts between pages: here Γ(d) = Σ^*(d ⊔ {ω}), while the margin of the next page writes Γ(n) = Σ^*(n+1), with n = {0,…,n}. These are consistent but easy to confuse.
The next page writes 'Γ(X) = Σ^*(0)', which should be Γ(∅). This is a slip on the neighbouring page, not this one.

ideas.what: Points of Σ^*(d) over x correspond to d-subsets of the local boundary germs, via increasing maps Δ_d → Δ_n with image A ∪ {n}. The germ at z maps onto the intersection of the corresponding B_α.
ideas.modern_name: k-fold boundary / corner spaces ∂^k X of a manifold with corners (local boundary components)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Douady (variétés à bord anguleux, 1961), Jänich, Laures (⟨n⟩-manifolds, 2000), Joyce (2009–2016)

ideas.what: Equivalence between the category of nonempty finite ordinals with last-element-preserving strictly increasing maps and the category of all finite ordinals (including ∅) with strictly increasing maps, via adjoining a last element ω.
ideas.modern_name: augmented semi-simplicial category Δ_+,inj realized as the max-preserving part of Δ_inj (the 'join with a point' trick)

ideas.what: Encoding an ordered, locally cylindrical stratification (corner structure) of Σ as an augmented semi-simplicial space over Σ whose fibres are full simplices on the local boundary germs. This is used to reconstruct the unfolding (déploiement) spaces.
ideas.modern_name: semi-simplicial/cubical nerve of the corner structure; cf. unzipping/resolution of stratified spaces to manifolds with corners
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (unzipping of conically smooth stratified spaces, 2017); Mather/Thom control data for tubular structures
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only alludes to tame topology and dévissage of stratified spaces, not to this construction

missed.claim: Grothendieck encodes an 'ordered' corner/stratification structure as an augmented semi-simplicial space Γ with Γ(∅) = Σ and Γ(d) = spaces of germs of codimension-(d+1) strata. The aim is to rebuild the unfolding (déploiement) of the stratified space from this simplicial datum. This anticipates the later 'unzipping' of stratified spaces into manifolds with corners (Ayala–Francis–Tanaka), and the semi-simplicial treatment of corner spaces ∂^k X (Joyce), within a single functorial packaging. This is not published or credited.
missed.quote: la donnée de ces foncteurs Γ revient à la donnée de Γ(∅) (ici Σ^*(0)) et d'un objet (espace) simplicial au-dessus de Γ(∅)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests describing manifolds with ordered faces/corners as augmented semi-simplicial objects with simplex fibres. This could give a clean simplicial characterization of 'ordered' corner structures, relevant to the stratified-spaces and ∞-categorical exit-path literature. It is a modest, mostly expository connection.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly routine combinatorics: the corner-subset correspondence and the max-preserving-maps equivalence with augmented semi-simplicial objects. The only notable aspect is the early (1981–82), unpublished programme of encoding stratified/corner structures as a relative semi-simplicial space in order to reconstruct the unfolding. This foreshadows later unzipping work, but the page itself contains no deep new result.
transcription_corrections: 'Σ^A(n)', 'Σ^A(d)', 'Σ^A(ω)' should read Σ^*(n), Σ^*(d), Σ^*(0) (the asterisk notation used throughout).
First line should read roughly: 'Δ_d dans Δ_n = {0,…,n} ayant pour image A ∪ {n}, et l'homomorphisme simplicial correspondant'.
The label over the arrows is likely 'induit' rather than 'immersion'.

'le groupe de sous-groupe de Σ^A(d) en z' should read 'le germe de Σ^*(d) en z'. Likewise 'l'image du germe de Σ^*(d) en z' and 'l'intersection des germes B_α correspondant aux z_α ∈ A', i.e. germes rather than groupes.
'sur les ens. tot. ordonnés [?] vides' should read 'sur les ens. tot. ordonnés éventuellement vides'.
'immersion' over the dashed arrow to Σ^*(0) should likewise be 'induite'.
